- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.11) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.17) and model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit above 0.17.
- Model frequently overestimates 30-day mean by 0.5–2% in early-week forecasts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% for first 5 days of forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.06–0.11) and price is near recent 10-day low, model often fails to recognize support; add 0.3–0.8% upward bias to avoid premature sell-off.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >1.5% for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence or sentiment shifts.
